_meta.what: Comparative dossier on the PROPERTY TAX regimes of six cities (Ahmedabad, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad) for 'The Unelected City' civic-accountability atlas. Property tax is the one major PROGRESSIVE, locally-controlled tax an elected corporation owns outright. The thesis (Cooper): it is chronically UNDER-assessed and UNDER-collected — held down by political resistance to revaluation — while cities lean instead on REGRESSIVE user fees, development charges and state transfers. The colonial hook (Ghosh): property/house tax WAS the original municipal base — 19c Calcutta's services were 'paid off from house taxes,' with householders bearing 59.5% of the burden while commerce was lightly taxed — so the regressive-on-residents pattern is inherited, not new.
_meta.rigor_tiers: A = DOCUMENTED FACT (city budgets, RBI 'Report on Municipal Finances' Nov 2024, Janaagraha ASICS, NIPFP/ICRIER, official property-tax rules/Acts). B = REPORTED, attributed (news/secondary). C = ANALYSIS.
_meta.authored: 2026-06, fresh run (two prior runs killed by infra errors wrote nothing; this file written early/incrementally). Figures are point-in-time, rounded, often year-mismatched across cities — municipal-finance data is patchy and lagged. Treat verify:true entries as less certain; gaps are flagged explicitly, NO fabrication.
_meta.assessment_system_split: THREE families. (1) ARV / Annual Rateable Value (colonial inheritance, rent-based, most manipulable): Chennai, Hyderabad. (2) Capital Value System (CVS, market-value based): Mumbai (2010). (3) Unit Area / area-based (formula: area x location/use factor x rate, removes assessor discretion): Bengaluru (UAV self-assessment 2000/2008), Kolkata (Unit Area Assessment, legislated 2017, rolled out 2017-2022), Ahmedabad (carpet-area-based since 2001).
_meta.key_contrast: ARV cities (Chennai, Hyderabad) are the most under-assessed because rateable value is frozen to notional fair rent and revisions are politically blocked; area/unit-area cities self-adjust better. But EVEN area-based cities under-collect because coverage (properties on the roll) lags the actual built stock by 20-50%.
_meta.rbi_2024_note: RBI 'Report on Municipal Finances' (Nov 2024) is the anchor (Tier A): municipal revenue receipts are just 0.6% of GDP (2023-24) vs 9.2% for the Centre and 14.6% for states. Own tax revenue (property + water + other local taxes) is only ~30% of total municipal revenue — the rest is state/central transfers and grants. Within own TAX revenue, property tax is dominant: property tax is >16% of TOTAL municipal-corporation revenue and >60% of OWN TAX revenue. But property tax is just 0.15% of India's GDP vs 1.7% in advanced economies — i.e., chronically under-collected. This is the fiscal substance of the '74th-Amendment-without-devolution' critique.

ahmedabad.assessment_system: Area-based (carpet-area) property tax. Tax = carpet area x base rate x factors (location/F1, age/F2, use/F3, occupancy/F4). Replaced the old ARV (annual rateable value) system.
ahmedabad.year_adopted: 2001 (AMC shifted from ARV to area-based capital/carpet-area system; one of the earliest Indian cities to do so).
ahmedabad.rate_basis: General tax on carpet area; base rate ~Rs 16/sq.m residential, ~Rs 28/sq.m non-residential, with water tax, conservancy/sewerage tax, education cess and fire tax loaded on top as components. Advance-payment rebate (~10-15%).
ahmedabad.key_exemptions: Religious/charitable trusts, government/diplomatic properties, properties below a minimal area threshold; rebates for advance/online payment and for women/senior owners in some years.
ahmedabad.collection_efficiency: Among the BEST of the six. AMC collected ~Rs 1,680 cr property tax in FY2023-24 (Tier A/B, news-sourced), up year-on-year, aided by aggressive recovery (sealing 2,300+ defaulter properties in a single drive) and an advance-payment rebate that pulls in ~Rs 800 cr+ early each year. Collection-to-demand commonly cited in the ~75-90% band in good years.
ahmedabad.coverage_gap: AMC ran GIS-based property surveys to bring untaxed properties onto the roll; historically a meaningful share were unassessed before the area-based + GIS reforms. Gap narrowed but not closed; ongoing sealing drives imply persistent defaulter/unassessed tail.
ahmedabad.share_of_own_revenue: Property tax is a leading own-TAX line, but AMC's own revenue is dominated by octroi-replacement / state GST compensation since octroi abolition. Per RBI 2024 pattern, property tax is the largest own-tax but own-tax is only ~30% of total. verify AMC-specific %.
ahmedabad.share_of_total_revenue: Modest — total revenue inflated by state grants and capital grants; property tax typically high-single-digit-to-low-teens % of total. verify.
ahmedabad.politics_note: Gujarat model: technocratic, GIS-driven, comparatively de-politicised collection — held up nationally as the reform exemplar. The area-based shift in 2001 deliberately removed assessor discretion that had enabled under-assessment.
ahmedabad.source: ahmedabadcity.gov.in property-tax rules; Gujarat Provincial Municipal Corporations Act; DeshGujarat/Prokeralanews (FY23-24 ~Rs 1,680 cr, FY24-25 rebate ~Rs 834 cr); RBI Report on Municipal Finances 2024; Janaagraha ASICS.

mumbai.assessment_system: Capital Value System (CVS) — tax based on market/ready-reckoner (Annual Statement of Rates) capital value of the property, replacing the old ARV (rateable value) regime.
mumbai.year_adopted: 2010 (CVS legislated/adopted; applied from FY2010-11; litigation over rules ran for years, Bombay HC / Supreme Court rulings 2019 struck down some retrospective rules).
mumbai.rate_basis: Tax = capital value x rate of tax; capital value = ready-reckoner rate x built-up area x weights (use, age, floor, construction type). Differentiated rates residential vs commercial.
mumbai.key_exemptions: Residential units up to 500 sq.ft (carpet) EXEMPTED from the tax component of property tax since 1 Jan 2022 (Shiv Sena pre-election decision) — costs BMC ~Rs 462 cr/yr in foregone revenue; waiver limit raised to 700 sq.ft in 2026 (further base erosion). Plus religious/charitable/government.
mumbai.collection_efficiency: BMC collected ~Rs 4,300 cr property tax in FY2023-24 against a ~Rs 4,500 cr target (Tier A/B). Large nominal demand but persistent arrears and big year-end recovery pushes; bills for FY23-24 were themselves DELAYED by the unresolved capital-value revision and refund exposure.
mumbai.coverage_gap: Significant — unauthorized/slum structures and the <500 (now <700) sq.ft exemption shrink the effective base. The mandatory 5-yearly capital-value revision was postponed past schedule (through 2023); the postponement alone cost ~Rs 1,080 cr in foregone revenue. SC ordered BMC to reframe rules and re-fix capital values; provisional bills issued.
mumbai.share_of_own_revenue: Since OCTROI abolition (2017, replaced by a state GST-compensation grant), property tax became one of BMC's largest INDEPENDENT own taxes — but BMC also leans heavily on income from its fixed deposits/investments and on the GST-compensation grant. verify precise %.
mumbai.share_of_total_revenue: Property tax roughly ~10-15% of BMC revenue income in recent budgets; the GST-compensation grant is the single largest line. verify.
mumbai.politics_note: The 500-then-700 sq.ft exemption and the repeated postponement of the mandatory 5-yearly capital-value revision are textbook blocked-revaluation politics — the base is frozen for electoral reasons, with the cost quantified by BMC itself (Rs 462 cr + Rs 1,080 cr).
mumbai.source: MCGM/BMC Capital Value Rules 2010/2015; Bombay HC & SC judgments 2019; taxguru/FreePressJournal (500 sq.ft exemption Rs 462 cr, FY23-24 ~Rs 4,300 cr, revision delay Rs 1,080 cr); MMC Act s.140A; RBI 2024; ASICS.

kolkata.assessment_system: Unit Area Assessment (UAA) — area-based formula (annual value = covered area x Base Unit Area Value of the block x multiplicative factors for location, use, age, occupancy, structure), replacing the colonial ARV system that had survived since the 19th century.
kolkata.year_adopted: Legislated via KMC (Amendment) Act 2016/2017; UAA notified and rolled out from 2017, made operative across categories through 2017-2022 (one of the LAST major cities to abandon ARV).
kolkata.rate_basis: Annual value (from unit-area formula) x rate of tax (progressive slab, ~6-20%) + howrah-bridge/other cess. Blocks classified into categories A-G by infrastructure/locality.
kolkata.key_exemptions: Religious/charitable, government, and small/low-value properties; rebates for timely/online payment. Bustee (slum) properties historically lightly assessed.
kolkata.collection_efficiency: Historically WEAK with huge accumulated arrears and a large litigation backlog, but RECOVERING: KMC reported ~Rs 1,258 cr property-tax collection in FY2024-25 (one of the higher municipal totals nationally), aided by an arrears-waiver scheme (50% off penalty, 40% off interest on dues older than 5 years) — itself an admission of a deep arrears stock. Collection-to-current-demand has long run below target. verify efficiency %.
kolkata.coverage_gap: Large — many properties carried the old frozen ARV through the slow 2017-2022 UAA migration; significant un-enumerated/under-valued stock, especially bustee (slum) and legacy tenanted property. The arrears-waiver scheme signals a base never fully brought current.
kolkata.share_of_own_revenue: Property tax is KMC's principal own-tax, but KMC own revenue is structurally weak and the corporation is heavily transfer/grant-dependent. verify precise %.
kolkata.share_of_total_revenue: Low; KMC runs persistent revenue stress with property tax a modest share of an already transfer-heavy total. verify.
kolkata.politics_note: The ~150-year persistence of colonial ARV until 2017 IS the politics — every attempt to move to area-based assessment was resisted for decades; UAA was finally legislated (2016/17) but rollout stayed slow and contested, then needed an arrears-waiver amnesty. Direct line to Ghosh's 19c house-tax base, where Calcutta's services were 'paid off from house taxes.'
kolkata.source: KMC Act 1980 & Amendment 2016/17 (UAA); KMC budget; egovtschemes/cleartax (FY24-25 ~Rs 1,258 cr, arrears-waiver scheme); Ghosh 2020 (colonial house-tax base); RBI 2024; ASICS.

chennai.assessment_system: Annual Rateable Value (ARV) — colonial rent-based system; tax derived from notional reasonable letting value (annual rental value) of the property. NOT moved to area/capital value.
chennai.year_adopted: ARV inherited from the colonial era (Chennai/Madras City Municipal Corporation Act 1919); still in force. The core city's general revision of ARV was last done in 1998; a 2013 GO to revise was issued and then STOPPED in 2019 — i.e., the base sat frozen for roughly two decades.
chennai.rate_basis: Half-yearly property tax = % of annual rental value (ARV), with components for general tax, education tax, library cess. ARV computed from per-sq.ft monthly Basic Street Rate (BSR) x plinth area x 12, minus depreciation.
chennai.key_exemptions: Owner-occupied residential get a rebate (~25% on ARV vs let-out); religious/charitable, government, ex-servicemen and certain small dwellings; central-government properties pay a service charge in lieu.
chennai.collection_efficiency: Moderate; Greater Chennai Corporation collection-to-demand commonly cited in the ~70-85% band — better than Kolkata, behind Ahmedabad. verify recent %.
chennai.coverage_gap: Material — the ~20-year gap between general revisions (1998 to the 2018-22 BSR exercise) meant assessed values lagged market reality badly; GCC ran enumeration/GIS drives to add unassessed properties and annexed-area stock (added areas revised 2008).
chennai.share_of_own_revenue: Property tax is GCC's largest own-tax revenue; but GCC depends substantially on state devolution/grants. verify precise %.
chennai.politics_note: The base was frozen from 1998; a 2013 revision GO was halted in 2019, and successive governments rolled back attempted hikes because 'residents were against the hike' (Madras School of Economics). The 2018-22 BSR revision was the first real reset in ~two decades and remained contentious. Classic ARV trap — fair rent frozen, revaluation electorally radioactive.
chennai.source: Chennai City Municipal Corporation Act 1919; GCC revenue dept & BSR schedule; Citizen Matters / Madras School of Economics (1998 last revision, 2013 GO stopped 2019, rollback pattern); RBI 2024; ASICS.

bengaluru.assessment_system: Unit Area Value (UAV) with SELF-ASSESSMENT Scheme (SAS) — taxpayer computes tax from published per-sq.ft unit-area rates by zone x built-up area x use/occupancy/age factors. Area-based, taxpayer-declared.
bengaluru.year_adopted: UAV/SAS introduced 2000, made mandatory/comprehensive 2008-09 (BBMP). Zonal classification keyed to Guidance Value; revision required every 3 years under the (old) KMC Act 1976 / now BBMP Act 2020.
bengaluru.rate_basis: Tax = UAV rate (Rs/sq.ft/month by zone, differing for self-occupied vs tenanted) x area x 10 months x rate of tax + cess (health, library, beautification). Self-occupied taxed lower than rented.
bengaluru.key_exemptions: Religious/charitable, government, heritage; vacant land taxed at lower rate; self-occupied concession vs let-out.
bengaluru.collection_efficiency: WEAK relative to potential. Janaagraha/ASICS recorded BBMP property-tax collection efficiency FALLING to 68% (2017-18) from 74-75% (2015-17). Self-assessment is widely gamed; a 2008-10 CAG sample found 40% of returns wrongly declared (Rs 207 cr loss in sample alone). verify latest %.
bengaluru.coverage_gap: VERY LARGE and the flagship case of self-assessment-enabled under-assessment. The 2024-25 e-Khata/e-Aasthi audit uncovered ~Rs 390 cr property-tax evasion across ~5 lakh properties (under-declared built-up area, residential rates misused for commercial use); a BBMP audit found roughly 1 in 7 buildings under-reports. CAG flagged that rates were not revised for over a decade (last rate revision 2000) despite a 3-yearly statutory mandate.
bengaluru.share_of_own_revenue: Property tax is BBMP's single largest own-revenue source (BBMP is comparatively own-revenue-reliant by Indian standards), but realized collection is far below assessed potential. verify precise %.
bengaluru.share_of_total_revenue: Property tax a leading share of BBMP revenue; verify exact.
bengaluru.politics_note: Self-assessment was sold as anti-corruption (removing inspector discretion) but produced systemic UNDER-declaration; rates went unrevised for over a decade against a 3-yearly mandate, and guidance values are politically frozen. BBMP's twin failure — to revise AND to enforce/verify — is the central Bengaluru story, quantified by CAG and the e-Khata audit.
bengaluru.source: BBMP Act 2020 & UAV/SAS rules; KMC Act 1976; CAG Karnataka Local Bodies audits 2009-10 & 2017; Deccan Herald/TheRealtyToday (e-Khata audit ~Rs 390 cr / ~5 lakh properties, 1-in-7 under-declares); Janaagraha ASICS (68% efficiency 2017-18); RBI 2024.

hyderabad.assessment_system: Annual Rental Value (ARV) — monthly-rental-value based; tax computed from per-sq.ft monthly rental value (MRV) by location x plinth area. Colonial-lineage rent-based system, NOT capital/area-value.
hyderabad.year_adopted: ARV inherited (Hyderabad Municipal Corporations Act 1955 / GHMC Act); MRV-slab method formalized; GHMC formed 2007 (amalgamation). Still ARV-based.
hyderabad.rate_basis: Annual property tax = 3.5 x plinth area x monthly rental value/sq.ft x (slab tax rate by ARV band, ~17-30% of ARV). Residential vs commercial MRV differ sharply.
hyderabad.key_exemptions: Properties with ARV/monthly rent below threshold EXEMPT (e.g., very low-rent small dwellings); religious/charitable, govt, ex-servicemen, recognized educational. Early-payment rebate.
hyderabad.collection_efficiency: Improving on the collection side — GHMC collected ~Rs 1,917 cr property tax in FY2023-24 (up from ~Rs 1,660 cr in FY22-23; Tier A/B), exceeding target in FY24-25 for the first time, helped by early-bird rebates and online/self-assessment drives. BUT arrears are enormous: ~Rs 5,500 cr outstanding, of which ~Rs 4,400 cr is owed by GOVERNMENT departments (secretariat, South Central Railway), some dating to 2001; ~7 lakh owners have not cleared dues in 8 years.
hyderabad.coverage_gap: Large — GHMC ran self-assessment + GIS drives to add un-enumerated and under-assessed properties; many commercial units assessed as residential. MRV frozen below market; the Rs 5,500 cr arrears stock is itself a coverage/enforcement failure, heavily concentrated in public-sector non-payers.
hyderabad.share_of_own_revenue: Property tax is GHMC's largest own-tax line; GHMC also leans on building-permission/development fees and state grants. verify precise %.
hyderabad.politics_note: MRV (monthly rental value) has been frozen far below market for years; general revision of MRV is repeatedly deferred for political reasons. The state's OWN departments are the biggest defaulters (Rs 4,400 cr) — the government will not pay the tax it sets. Self-assessment + rebate drives substitute for the politically impossible base revaluation. Classic ARV trap shared with Chennai.
hyderabad.source: GHMC Act / Hyderabad Municipal Corporations Act 1955; GHMC property-tax rules (MRV slabs); propnewstime/proptaxlekka (FY23-24 ~Rs 1,917 cr, Rs 5,500 cr arrears incl. Rs 4,400 cr govt); RBI 2024; ASICS.
